standing: PROPOSED D2 description-batch contract successor (law VD1 r1 item 6; EXIT-PLAN D1 note): explicit supersessions of the effective descriptions of 4 inherited rows of repository-file-inventory.v122.json whose text no longer describes the file at product 96dd114; description-only, no schema, registry, generated code, inventory or product change; exact frozen candidate requires actual independent review and root assent.

passageSupersessions.before: Own alloc-only full-triple lineage keys, the one relative node spelling transitions/lineage/S/G/K.node that every crate joins, closed canonical 4096-byte node decoding and bounded iterative supplied-chain inspection. Callers assemble OS paths from those components; the spelling is not resolution. Decoded chains do not prove native existence, publication, complete operation budget or authority.
passageSupersessions.after: Own alloc-only full-triple lineage keys, the one relative node spelling transitions/lineage/S/G/K.node that every crate joins, closed canonical 4096-byte node decoding and bounded iterative supplied-chain inspection. Callers assemble OS paths from those components; the spelling is not resolution. SuppliedChain::into_nodes yields the inspected chain by value, selected node to root, so that the write gate's one read and the observation session's member reads keep it for the selected store endpoint (law X3a items 2 and 3, unit X3a-1). Decoded chains do not prove native existence, publication, complete operation budget or authority.

passageSupersessions.before: The read side's observation path (law 458c r5 items 5, 6, 7 and 11). One session per process on one failure-latching ledger with the owner's limits; one observation per session. It reaches I through the durable write gate's own step 0 and step 1 code, shared rather than copied, with no barrier: a charged, retained, no-follow walk from the root to I under the read receipt's sealed lending, a positive absence only when the first missing suffix component is observed absent under its retained parent, and lifecycle.fence opened through the retained I. The lock wait repeats one nonblocking attempt on that same descriptor, paced at 25 ms, for at most 5 s and 201 attempts, all reserved before the first; busy retries, any other failure stops on the host I/O row, and a lock still busy at the bound is the busy row. Under the held fence it runs the receipt's rechecks and the full recheck set, reads the required members charged before they run (the fixed members up front, each lineage node before its own read), records missing, undecodable or misbound members as structural findings, and runs the same full recheck over every captured file, also after a failed read. Every refusal takes exactly the write gate's row. Never a write capability. Its consumers are the read session behind InstallationReadFence::acquire and doctor's installation check. Library only: no CLI command is wired.
passageSupersessions.after: The read side's observation path (law 458c r5 items 5, 6, 7 and 11). One session per process on one failure-latching ledger with the owner's limits; one observation per session. It reaches I through the durable write gate's own step 0 and step 1 code, shared rather than copied, with no barrier: a charged, retained, no-follow walk from the root to I under the read receipt's sealed lending, a positive absence only when the first missing suffix component is observed absent under its retained parent, and lifecycle.fence opened through the retained I. The lock wait repeats one nonblocking attempt on that same descriptor, paced at 25 ms, for at most 5 s and 201 attempts, all reserved before the first; busy retries, any other failure stops on the host I/O row, and a lock still busy at the bound is the busy row. Under the held fence it runs the receipt's rechecks and the full recheck set, reads the required members charged before they run (the fixed members up front, each lineage node before its own read), records missing, undecodable or misbound members as structural findings, and runs the same full recheck over every captured file, also after a failed read. The receipt's rechecks run again after that final recheck. Within the same one read (law X3a items 1 to 5, unit X3a-1): the selection pair must name the read receipt's selected core, or it is the core finding; the trust current record trust/stores/S/state.v1 is read once under CURRENT_STATE_CAP and decoded, and a record over its cap, undecodable or naming a store other than the pair's is the current-store finding; a lineage chain longer than its generation allows is a finding, while the session's own node limit is the budget row; and a complete I keeps the endpoint values (the pair, the marker, the node chain and the current record) for the selected store endpoint. retain (unit 458c-b2) requires I complete and keeps the observation, the receipt and the session's ledger in the ReadSession. Every refusal takes exactly the write gate's row. Never a write capability. Its consumers are the read session behind InstallationReadFence::acquire and doctor's installation check. Its one wired CLI path is opensip doctor (law X10), through doctor's installation check.

passageSupersessions.before: Produce the read side's premise receipt (law 458c r5 items 1 to 4): the process's one attempt, the actor, InitialCore and InitialPlatform, exactly the creator's producers, with no intent, storage choice, disclosure, effect or fence. The receipt is private and not Clone, holds its own attempt, and lends only the sealed ReadPremiseQualification that InitialPlatform alone implements: the check that a filesystem is H's and the omission premise with 465 item 4's scope, no barrier policy. Every refusal ends in its law 468 item 6 row through 468c's maps. InstallationReadFence::acquire and doctor's installation check pass it to the observation session. Library only: no CLI command is wired.
passageSupersessions.after: Produce the read side's premise receipt (law 458c r5 items 1 to 4): the process's one attempt, the actor, InitialCore and InitialPlatform, exactly the creator's producers, with no intent, storage choice, disclosure, effect or fence. Law X1 r1 items 1 and 2 type it by purpose: the one producer composition makes PlatformReceipt<Read> (ReadPremiseReceipt, produce_read_platform) or PlatformReceipt<Write> (WritePlatformReceipt, produce_write_platform); Read and Write are sealed, neither receipt converts into the other, and a receipt whose actor, core or platform belongs to another attempt is the invariant row. The read receipt is private and not Clone, holds its own attempt, and lends only the sealed ReadPremiseQualification that InitialPlatform alone implements: the check that a filesystem is H's and the omission premise with 465 item 4's scope, no barrier policy. The write receipt is likewise private, not Clone and holds its own attempt; its lending is the durable write gate's sealed DurableBarrierQualification, beside which it lends the running core's embedded bootstrap source to the fenced first read alone (law X4B r5 item 2, unit X4B-b), charge, one charged step on its attempt ledger with that lending (unit X2e), charge_guarded, the same step with the actor, core and platform rechecks lent beside it for the checkpoint's guard (law X4 r7 item 4, unit X4a), and the attempt ledger's one end-path settlement reserve and its single spend, on the commit session's way only (law X3d r6 item 8, unit X3d-1). Both purposes expose recheck, the actor, core and platform rechecks on the receipt's own attempt, and selected_core, the selected core's closure and state writer K as values only (law X3a item 1). Every refusal ends in its law 468 item 6 row through 468c's maps. InstallationReadFence::acquire and doctor's installation check pass it to the observation session. The ordinary writer's admission consumes the write receipt (law X1), and the operation handoff carries it (unit X2e). Its one wired CLI path is opensip doctor (law X10), through doctor's installation check; no CLI command reaches a write receipt.

passageSupersessions.before: Own the initial creator's pre-installation attempt: one per process, the only work ledger for the whole act and a failure latch, with private non-Clone receipts bound to the attempt. Mint the InitialActor (equal real and effective UID, a plain absolute home spelling that fits I within 4096 bytes and 256 components) and recheck it; classify storage (constant UNKNOWN), apply the first-creation backup choice, write and flush the first-write disclosure, and mint, recheck and consume the single-use CreationIntent with its request and execution ids at StepId 0. It opens no installation path, creates nothing, and does not enable the creator.
passageSupersessions.after: Own the initial creator's pre-installation attempt: one per process, the only work ledger for the whole act and a failure latch, with private non-Clone receipts bound to the attempt. The same attempt, with its one ledger, is also the process's one attempt behind the read receipt and the ordinary writer's write receipt (laws 458c and X1). Mint the InitialActor (equal real and effective UID, a plain absolute home spelling that fits I within 4096 bytes and 256 components) and recheck it; classify storage (constant UNKNOWN), apply the first-creation backup choice, write and flush the first-write disclosure, and mint, recheck and consume the single-use CreationIntent with its request and execution ids at StepId 0. recheck_actor_in rechecks the actor on a borrowed scope (law 467 item 6; also the write receipt's guard, law X4 r7 item 4), and recheck_storage_in and recheck_handoff_storage rebuild I and re-classify a consumed intent's target (law 467 item 2). reserve_end_path_settlement takes the attempt ledger's one settlement reserve, refused Closed once the attempt is latched, and settle_end_path spends it once whether or not the attempt is latched (law X3d r6 item 8, unit X3d-1); they are the only production callers of WorkLedger::reserve_settlement and settle, reached only on the write receipt's way to the commit session's end-path step and StoppedSession::finish. It opens no installation path, creates nothing, and does not enable the creator.
